Somerville.narrative: Somerville's housing market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with condos and multi-families leading the charge — 42.5% and 42.9% of those sales, respectively, closed above asking price, while the median condo sale hit $992,500 and multi-families commanded a $1,300,000 median. Single-family homes are the priciest segment at a $1,699,000 median, though with only 5 sales in the past 30 days and a 95.8% sale-to-list ratio, that slice of the market is both thin and slightly more negotiable by Somerville standards. Inventory is essentially nonexistent across all categories, meaning buyers should expect to move fast, come in strong with pre-approvals, and be prepared to waive contingencies to stay competitive. For sellers, conditions are about as favorable as they get — particularly in the condo and multi-family space where bidding wars are the clear norm — making this an excellent window to maximize returns.

Cambridge.narrative: Cambridge remains one of the most fiercely competitive markets in Greater Boston, with single-family homes commanding a median of $2.3M and selling at 104.2% of list price — a staggering 81.8% of those sales closing above asking. The condo market is nearly as active, with 67 units trading hands in the past 30 days at a median of $1.1M and an even 100% SP/LP ratio, while multi-families fetched a median of $1.65M with a third of those also attracting above-ask offers. With effectively zero months of supply across all property types, inventory is critically constrained, leaving buyers facing intense bidding wars and little room to negotiate. Sellers, by contrast, are in an exceptionally strong position — properly priced homes are moving quickly and generating multiple offers, making this an ideal window to capitalize on Cambridge's enduring demand driven by its proximity to Harvard, MIT, and the broader innovation economy.

Medford.narrative: Medford's housing market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single families commanding a median of $950,000 and closing at 102.7% of list price — 69.2% of those homes selling above asking, a clear signal that buyer demand is overwhelming available supply. Condos are slightly more forgiving at a $825,000 median and a 99.4% SP/LP ratio, though still moving briskly with 19 units sold in the past 30 days and just over a quarter going above list price. Multi-family properties, while thinly traded with only 2 sales, are posting the most aggressive numbers — a $1,330,000 median and a striking 107.2% SP/LP ratio with half selling over ask, reflecting strong investor and house-hacker demand in this transit-accessible city. For buyers, the near-zero months of supply means coming in with your best offer from the start, while sellers across all categories are in an exceptional position to price confidently and expect strong, fast results.

Melrose.narrative: Melrose continues to command serious buyer attention across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $1,031,800 and an average of 105.7% of list price — meaning buyers are routinely paying $50,000 or more above asking, with nearly 79% of homes selling over list. The inventory picture is essentially nonexistent with no measurable months of supply across all segments, and multi-family properties are seeing the sharpest competition of all, with every single one of the 3 sales in the past 30 days closing above asking at a median of $820,000. Condos offer a relatively softer entry point at a $640,000 median with sales landing right at list price on average, though two-thirds still sold over ask, signaling that even the "calmer" segment is no buyer's market. For sellers, Melrose is about as favorable as it gets — price confidently and expect multiple offers — while buyers should come in pre-approved, waiver-ready, and prepared to move fast with strong escalation clauses.

Arlington.narrative: Arlington's real estate market is running extremely hot across all property types, with single-family homes posting a median sale price of $1,222,778 and selling at 107.4% of list price — nearly three-quarters of them closing above asking. Condos are slightly more measured at a $929,000 median with an even 100% sale-to-list ratio, though still a third of units are trading over ask, while multi-families are the most competitive segment of all, with a $1,522,500 median and a striking 115.4% sale-to-list ratio and every single one of the 4 sales in the past 30 days going above asking price. With essentially zero months of supply across the board, sellers hold enormous leverage and can expect strong offers — often multiple — within days of listing. Buyers should come prepared with pre-approvals in hand, meaningful escalation clauses, and a willingness to waive contingencies, as hesitation in Arlington almost certainly means losing out to a competing offer.

Belmont.narrative: Belmont's real estate market is firing on all cylinders, with single-family homes commanding a median sale price of $1,557,500 and an extraordinary 87.5% of properties selling above asking price at an average of 105% of list price — a clear signal that demand is vastly outpacing supply, which sits at effectively zero months. Condos offer a comparatively accessible entry point at a $592,000 median, though even that segment sees half of all units closing over ask at 101.4% SP/LP, while multi-families are fetching a robust $1,431,000 median with 66.7% selling above list. For buyers, this means coming in with strong pre-approvals, meaningful escalation clauses, and minimal contingencies just to stay competitive across all property types. Sellers, meanwhile, are in an enviable position — the razor-thin inventory and aggressive buyer competition in Belmont are consistently producing sale prices well beyond expectations, making this one of the most landlord-friendly listing environments in Greater Boston right now.

Watertown.narrative: Watertown's real estate market remains intensely competitive across all property types, with single families commanding a median of $1,005,000 and closing at 100.5% of list price — two-thirds of those homes selling above asking. Condos are slightly more forgiving at a $695,460 median with an even 100% SP/LP ratio, though still over half are going above list, while the multi-family segment is the hottest of all, with both sales in the past 30 days closing above ask at a striking 103.6% SP/LP and a median of $997,500. With effectively zero months of supply across every category, inventory is the defining constraint right now. For sellers, this is about as favorable an environment as it gets — properly priced homes are generating immediate, competitive offers — while buyers should expect to move fast, come in strong, and budget meaningfully above list price to have a realistic shot in any segment.

Winchester.narrative: Winchester's single-family market is commanding serious attention, with a median sale price of $1,830,000 and homes closing at 100.9% of list price — 61.1% of them selling above asking within the last 30 days across 18 transactions. The condo segment is even more competitive, with a median of $930,000, a 103.7% sale-to-list ratio, and a striking 83.3% of units closing over ask across 6 sales. With effectively zero months of supply in both segments, inventory is critically tight, giving sellers exceptional pricing power and the ability to expect multiple offers with favorable terms. Buyers should be prepared to move fast, waive contingencies strategically, and come in above list price — especially on condos — to have any realistic chance of securing a home in this high-demand town.

Boston.narrative: Boston's real estate market remains fiercely competitive across all property types, with single-family homes leading the charge at a median sale price of $886,000 and an impressive 101.7% sale-to-list ratio, meaning nearly 63% of homes are selling above asking price. The condo market continues to show remarkable volume with 316 sales in the last 30 days at a median of $797,500, while multi-families command a hefty $1,082,500 median — reflecting strong investor and owner-occupant demand, with over half selling above list. With effectively zero months of supply across all segments, this is an unambiguously seller's market where well-priced properties are generating multiple offers and above-ask results almost as a matter of course. Buyers should come prepared with strong pre-approvals, flexible terms, and the mindset to move decisively, as hesitation in this environment almost certainly means losing out.
